approach: In `validate_item` (crates/athena-core/src/steward.rs), after the evidence references are checked and before the rung and request checks, count the distinct validated evidence references and refuse a non-blind-spot item with fewer than two (new const MIN_EVIDENCE = 2). The reason names the key and says one instance is not a general weakness. Blind spots return earlier in the function, so they stay exempt. Raise the shared `item()` test helper to two evidence references and fix the three tests that assert one. Add one new unit test for the refusal and for duplicates counting once. Fill OLY-5-07's mechanism in docs/spec.toml and set its measure to `cargo test -p athena-core steward; status: not shown`. Add enforcement row M34 and a CHANGELOG entry.

decisions.choice: Count distinct validated `Reference` values (after `check_reference` trims them) with a Vec and `contains`; require at least 2 (`MIN_EVIDENCE`). Place the check after the evidence is validated, before the rung and request checks.
decisions.reason: `Reference` derives only Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize and Deserialize (crates/athena-data/src/records/work.rs:18), so it cannot go in a HashSet or BTreeSet without changing the data crate. A list of at most a few items makes a linear contains cheap. Checking after validation means a malformed reference reports its own error first, and ' k7q2 ' and 'k7q2' count once.

rejected.option: Count raw item.evidence entries before validation
rejected.why: Duplicates and whitespace variants of one job would pass, which is the one-off the rule exists to refuse.

rejected.option: Derive Hash/Ord on Reference in athena-data
rejected.why: It widens the change to a second crate for a list of a few entries.

rejected.option: Add the source reference to the evidence count
rejected.why: The source says where the proposal came from, not what shows the weakness is general. Counting it would let one cited job pass.

decisions.choice: Keep the empty-evidence message and check ahead of the new check. The new check has its own reason text.
decisions.reason: The existing test `invalid_items_are_dropped_with_a_reason_and_do_not_stop_the_rest` expects eight rejections, and keeping both checks keeps that count at eight. Zero evidence and one evidence are different faults to report.

rejected.option: Replace the empty check with 'fewer than two'
rejected.why: It loses the specific zero-evidence message that existing callers may read.

decisions.choice: Exempt blind spots by leaving the early return as is.
decisions.reason: A blind spot is Athena's own report that a source cannot be read. Its evidence is the source name (steward.rs:779, or empty at line 761), and its key and rung are Athena's.

rejected.option: Apply the rule to all kinds
rejected.why: The existing blind-spot tests clear the evidence and expect acceptance (lines 1849, 1868, 2229), and the brief says blind spots are exempt.

decisions.choice: Leave the steward brief and role prompt text alone.
decisions.reason: Changing prompts and role definitions is out of scope. The refusal reason is recorded in `Validated.rejected` and reaches the run report (steward.rs:1304).

rejected.option: Add 'cite at least two' to the brief at steward.rs:1128 and 1424

files.purpose: Add `MIN_EVIDENCE` and the distinct-evidence check in `validate_item`; raise the `item()` helper and the JSON/assertion tests to two references; add the new unit test.
OLY-5-07 only: set the mechanism to the new rule in `validate_item` and the measure to `cargo test -p athena-core steward; status: not shown`. Owner stays Athena.
Add an entry under [Unreleased] / Added for the rule.
Add row M34: a steward proposal needs two distinct evidence references; names the blocking and allowing tests.

steps: In crates/athena-core/src/steward.rs, next to MAX_REQUEST (~line 842), add `/// The fewest distinct evidence references a non-blind-spot item may cite: one instance is not a general weakness.` and `const MIN_EVIDENCE: usize = 2;`.

In `validate_item`, after `let evidence = ...?;` (line ~998) and before `let rung = ladder(item.rung);`, build `let mut distinct: Vec<&Reference> = Vec::new();`, push each reference not already contained, and if `distinct.len() < MIN_EVIDENCE` return `Err(format!("{key}: evidence holds {n} distinct reference(s); one instance is not a general weakness, so cite at least {MIN_EVIDENCE}"))`. Keep the existing empty-evidence check above it. Do not touch the blind-spot branch.

Update the tests. In `item()` (line ~1992) add a second `StewardRefOutput { kind: RefKindOutput::Path, value: "records/jobs".into() }` after the job entry. In `a_valid_item_becomes_a_proposed_change` (line ~2020) assert evidence equals the job reference and `Reference::path("records/jobs")`. In `the_steward_output_parser_reads_the_five_brief_fields` (line ~1886) add a second evidence object, a path reference. Leave `change()` and the `decide` tests alone since they bypass validation. Confirm that `unknown_job` and `bad_commit` still fail on their own reference error.

Add the test `one_instance_is_not_a_general_weakness` after `invalid_items_are_dropped_with_a_reason_and_do_not_stop_the_rest`. Cases: (a) a repeated-failure item and a proposal item with one evidence reference, each refused with a reason containing the key and `not a general weakness`; (b) one job cited twice, once with surrounding spaces, refused; (c) a job plus a path accepted; (d) a blind spot with empty evidence accepted. Then confirm the test fails with the check commented out, and restore the check.

In docs/spec.toml, change only the OLY-5-07 row: mechanism = "validate_item in crates/athena-core/src/steward.rs refuses a repeated-failure or proposal item that cites fewer than two distinct evidence references, so one instance is not treated as a general weakness; blind spots are exempt."; owner stays "Athena"; measure = "cargo test -p athena-core steward; status: not shown".

In docs/enforcement.md add row M34 after M33: rule 'A steward proposal needs general evidence, not one instance (OLY-5-07)'; mechanism `validate_item` in steward.rs with `MIN_EVIDENCE`; blocks `one_instance_is_not_a_general_weakness`; allows `a_valid_item_becomes_a_proposed_change`. Add to CHANGELOG.md under [Unreleased] / Added a bullet about the rule, naming OLY-5-07 and the exempt blind spots.

Run `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --locked`, `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus` and `cargo test -p xtask`. Report which passed.

risks.risk: A genuine one-off the steward should still raise (a proposal citing a single decisive job) is now refused.
risks.mitigation: This is the stated requirement. The refusal is recorded in `rejected` with the key and the reason, and the rule is one const (`MIN_EVIDENCE`) the owner can change. Blind spots are exempt.

risks.risk: The steward's prompt does not say that two references are needed, so early runs may lose items to the new rule.
risks.mitigation: Prompts are out of scope here. The reason text tells the next reader what is missing, and the CHANGELOG entry says so. The user can approve a later prompt change.

risks.risk: The rule counts references, not whether they show the same failure, so two weak references pass.
risks.mitigation: The check is a floor, not a judgment of quality; the existing rung, request and critic checks still apply. The measure is `status: not shown`, so no claim is made beyond the test.

risks.risk: A new row in docs/enforcement.md breaks xtask if a test name is misspelled.
risks.mitigation: Step 6 copies the test names from the new test and the edited existing test. `cargo test -p xtask` is in the verification commands.

demonstrations.observes: The OLY-5-07 row has mechanism text naming validate_item in crates/athena-core/src/steward.rs, owner "Athena", and a measure `cargo test -p athena-core steward; status: not shown`. `the_real_spec_passes` reports no 'no mechanism', 'no measure' or 'no measure label' error for OLY-5-07.

demonstrations.method: Unit test in steward.rs's `mod tests` calls `validate_items` (which calls the private `validate_item`) with a `Records` fixture from `records_with_job`. The test builds a repeated-failure item and a proposal item with the shared `item()` helper trimmed to one evidence reference.
demonstrations.observes: A one-evidence repeated-failure item and a one-evidence proposal item each land in `rejected` with a reason that contains the key and `not a general weakness`, and `changes` stays empty. The same items with a second distinct reference are accepted. A blind-spot item with empty evidence is still accepted.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the check, the one-evidence items are accepted. `valid.rejected` is empty and the `contains("not a general weakness")` assertion fails.
demonstrations.seam: Entry point `validate_items` -> `validate_item` (steward.rs:932,954), called directly from the in-file test module. The fixture is `records_with_job` (exists, steward.rs:1970) and the `item()` helper (exists, steward.rs:1982; step 3 changes it to two references). No double: the real code runs.

demonstrations.method: The same new test also builds an item whose two evidence entries are the same job (once with surrounding spaces) and asserts it is refused. Removing the new check from `validate_item` makes the test fail, and putting it back makes it pass. The producer checks this by temporarily commenting out the check, running the test, then restoring it.
demonstrations.observes: The duplicate-reference item is refused, with the rejection counting one distinct reference. A path reference and a job reference make two distinct references and are accepted.
demonstrations.fails_without: The test fails at its first assertion when the new check is absent, because the single-evidence and duplicate-evidence items are accepted. It passes with the check present.
demonstrations.seam: Same entry point and fixtures as criterion 2: `validate_items` with `records_with_job` (exists). The step-4 test adds the cases. No double.

open_questions: User: Is 'two distinct evidence references' the right test for a demonstrated general weakness? A stricter test, such as two distinct jobs, would also refuse a job plus a path. This plan takes the reading's rule: any two distinct references of any kind.
